title: Anyone actually making money off of your games?
author: Happy_Magazine4086
selftext: Planning to start making iOS and android games maybe in browser ones too, and I like what I’m seeing but just wondering if anyone is actually making money off of these and feel free to drop your games and promote yourselves in the comments I’d be happy to check them out regardless of how much you’ve made :)

comments.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
comments.body:
That's the problem.  
The jump from "interesting idea the AI prototyped in 20 min" to "Actually fun game that looks polished" is enormous.

And even if you reach the later, getting people to give it a shot is difficult especially with all the AI hate.

replies.author: Happy_Magazine4086
replies.body: Yes totally agree, initially my game was terrible, animation, art, mechanics after spending about a week on it I could see how someone might find this fun. The reason I’m asking is I want to know if it’s worth the effort to actually polish this up over a month or so

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
I am in the same boat...

Tbh i bet the most "realistic path" is reaching a stade where videos of your gameplay can genuinely hook people, make some sort of steam page "comming soon" of it with a good demo, work on marketing it a bit, and once you got enough wishlist boom a release.

But realistically... maybe a few hundred sales, and then downvotes because "AI bad".

Maybe i am wrong tho. Likely depends on how good the game truly is.

replies.author: Impressive_Award_679
replies.body: First yes, second no. New studies have proven that only 8% of all "ai haters" wouldnt buy a game if it is obviously AI made. 8% is literally nothing for a "indie dev" and most of the time not even the target audience.

replies.body: I dont think its a matter of "how much" isntead of "how good does the game looks". If its looks like the most generic AI game, than yes, more people will not buy it. If it just looks like a nice game, the most people just dont care. This statistics show that people in the first place care about if a game looks like a funny game for them and not if its made with AI or not.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Unfortunately mobile is not a place you can make money without getting extremely lucky or having a huge marketing budget. Competition is brutal.  Everyone is going after a small group of whales.

replies.author: Happy_Magazine4086
replies.body: So where do you think the money is at?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body:
Not in games TBH

If you want to make money with AI I would guess games is one of the harder ways to do it.

replies.author: ScutFarkush
replies.body: i think it probably makes it easier, but the bottleneck is going to be a good game idea, that feels polished, and then marketing. so if you have a good idea and arent trying to finish the game in a weirdly compressed timeline(i am 6 months into my game and it finally is starting to feel good and look good enough to have people play test)

replies.author: Orlandogameschool
replies.body:
Lots of money in games. Think outside the box

Sell your game to a business.

Package it as a website landing page to a small business that doesn’t have a website: now it’s a valuable fancy lead generation tool.

With a Game in the middle.

Research “gamification”

I made a pizza shop /paper boy themed for my friends pizza shop, and a trash collection game for another friend. I’m working on a lot of “boring” games like roofing and security.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Also the actual lift in mobile gaming is long term support of a microtx laden game as a service.  It's easy to make a templated gacha game, it's hard to foster a playerbase that wants to hand you money week after week to feed their unhealthy gambling addiction.  The actual success is mostly tied to existing IP as well.

It's now your full time job to churn out content on a weekly cadence and do customer support.  That's not a "spit out AI slop game, turn on infinite money fountain" pipeline like the people like OP think it is.

It's always wild to see people thinking gaming in general is some easy money get rich quick scheme.  Game dev is much closer to the starving artist stereotypes, it's a labor of love that maybe some people get lucky and make money off of.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body:
Exactly, I make some money off of one of my games but if you take into account the hours of my life I put into that and previous/subsequent games it's hardly a good way to make a living. 

People see the occasional success stories of single dev indie games and forget about the 10s of thousands of failed indie games that don't even recoup their steam fee.

comments.author: USDJPYFX
comments.body: It’s hard and it’s only going to get harder. The flood gates have been opened.

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744

I agree with this.  
In 1 year or less it will be so easy to make a decent looking game that everything will be flooded by "decent looking games", and it will become hard to stand out.

You shouldn‘t view this as a way to make money  
Making games should be enjoyable in the process, and you should make a game you enjoy

comments.author: Zeiban
comments.body:
In the past, wannabe game designers  didn't have the technical know-how to get to the prototype stage. Now they can and most are realizing that they're not great game designers.  

Creating a game that is unique that people find fun and want to play is extremely hard and not something AI is going to be able to figure out for you.  

So I don't think it's a matter of not being able to make money creating games with AI. It's still comes down to being able to create a good game regardless of whether you use AI or not.
